claims.source: TR-AC-47 title page, rendered from the scan at https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/SilverBug/AFD-070114-006.pdf
claims.text: The title page reads 'TR-AC-47 / (Unclassified) / JOINT ATIC-WADC REPORT ON / PROJECT SILVER BUG / PROJECT NO. 9961 / 15 FEBRUARY 1955', issued by the 'AIR TECHNICAL INTELLIGENCE CENTER, WRIGHT-PATTERSON AIR FORCE BASE, OHIO', and carries a handwritten declassification stamp reading 'Declassified 29 MAR 95', 'Auth: DoD 5200.1.R', 'SAF/AAZD'.

The report's Summary states its purpose: 'This report presents factual technical data on A. V. Roe, Canada, Limited, proposed development, Project Y2 (Secret)... The ultimate purpose of presenting this is two-fold; to correct the distorted picture presented in previous releases, both classified and unclassified, and to acquaint the intelligence community with the current state-of-the-art facts thereby alerting them to any air intelligence information which may become available indicating Soviet interest in this specialized field.'

The Summary's Discussion section states: 'This project should in no way be associated with any science fiction or "Flying Saucer" stories because of its external appearance. The configuration was a result of an engineering investigation into the solution of a particular problem.' It names the contractor as 'AVRO Aircraft, Limited, a member of the Hawker-Siddley Group'.

claims.source: TR-AC-47, page 1, Section I B 1, General Description, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/SilverBug/AFD-070114-006.pdf
claims.text: Section I distinguishes the two company designations: 'Two versions of small research VTO aircraft have been designed by the contractor, which, by company designation, are Project Y (Secret), a "tail-sitter", and Project Y2 (Secret), a "flat-riser". Early in the investigation, Project Y (Secret) was rejected by the contractor in favor of the flat-riser.'

Table III, 'CONTRACTOR ESTIMATED PERFORMANCE, Radial-Flow Engine Aircraft', gives Mach 2.6 and a 71,600 ft ceiling without reheat and Mach 3.48 and an 80,600 ft ceiling with 1500 degrees K reheat. The report qualifies these on page 17: 'The performance estimated by the contractor was based on rather broad assumptions and has not as yet been investigated by a wind tunnel test program.'

claims.source: TR-AC-47, page 23, Section II B, Present Development Status, https://documents.theblackvault.com/documents/SilverBug/AFD-070114-006.pdf
claims.text: Section II dates the USAF development track: Technical Requirement No. 3 dated 13 August 1954, a development plan dated 15 September 1954 written by 'WADC, Directorate of Weapons Systems Operations, Bombardment Aircraft Division, New Development Office', an order to proceed issued 29 December 1954, and a proposed statement of work dated 8 November 1954 to be incorporated in a study contract.

The report names the Coanda effect but not Henri Coanda: Figure 15 is 'Coanda Effect: High Aspect Ratio Jet Bending' and page 17 describes 'the so-called "Coanda effect" whereby a jet stream is deflected through large angles by having a curved surface in contact with its edge at one side'. No individual designer is named anywhere in the pages read, and the string 'Frost' does not appear in them.

desc: A joint report of the Air Technical Intelligence Center and the Wright Air Development Center on a Canadian contractor's proposal for a supersonic circular-planform aircraft with vertical take-off. It is the cleanest documented instance on this board of the Air Force funding a disc-shaped aircraft at Wright-Patterson, and its own stated purpose is to stop the intelligence community from believing the exaggerated accounts already circulating about it. It is the control case any Wright-Patterson recovery claim has to clear, and it is cited in the Michels corpus for the opposite of what it says: the transcript frames the project as a funnel and cover for deeper theoretical physics, while the report exists 'to correct the distorted picture presented in previous releases, both classified and unclassified' and says the project 'should in no way be associated with any science fiction or "Flying Saucer" stories because of its external appearance'. John Frost is named nowhere in it, the report names no individual designer at all, and the contractor is A. V. Roe, Canada, Limited, of the Hawker-Siddley Group, not the British Aircraft Corporation, which did not exist in 1955.

timeline.label: ATIC and WADC report jointly on a disc-shaped supersonic aircraft
timeline.text: TR-AC-47, Project No. 9961, is issued at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base on the Avro Canada Project Y2 flat-riser. Its stated purpose is to correct the distorted picture presented in previous releases and to alert the intelligence community to any Soviet interest, and its Summary says the project should in no way be associated with any science fiction or flying saucer stories because of its external appearance. It was declassified on 29 March 1995.
